sentences.text: 1 The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 22.03.2020.

2. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 22.03.2020 at about 06.30 p.m., while petitioner was proceeding in the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-05- KP-7440 as pillion rider, on Kanakapura- Bangalore main road i.e., from Harohalli and proceeding towards Kaggalipura, Bangalore along with his friend Santhosh Kumar.

The rider of the said motorcycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 53-EE-9901, caused the accident and as a result, petitioner sustained grievous injuries to his face, nose and head.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Cura hospital wherein he took treatment for the accidental injuries sustained by him.

It is stated that he has spent more than Rs.15,00,000/- for his treatment, medicine etc.,
3.
It is further stated that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as Helper under several Electrical Contractors and earning Rs.18,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not able to do his work as doing earlier.

It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-05-KP-7440.
Hence, the 1st and 2nd respondents being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 entered its appearance through its learned counsel and filed the objection statement.
The respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court even after service of notice, hence he has been placed exparte.
5. The 1st respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
The 2nd respondent has denied the age, income, occupation and medical expenses spent by the petitioner.

It has also denied the alleged negligence of the rider of the motorcycle and contended that the accident has occurred only due to the negligence on the part of the rider of another motor cycle bearing No.KA-55-EE-9901.

The respondent No.1 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-KP-7440 and contended that its liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
2nd respondent has further contended that the rider of the motorcycle was not holding valid D.L at the time of accident.
It has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, on all these grounds sought for dismissal of the petition.
6. Based on the pleadings, following issues are framed:-

If so, to what amount and from whom?

No.
KA-05-KP-7440, near Gandhinagar Petrol bunk, Uttarahalli hobli, Bengaluru, the rider of said motorcycle by riding it in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA- 53-EE-9901, caused the accident and as a result, petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.

Further the above documents also clearly discloses that the charge sheet is filed against offending motorcycle No.KA-05-KP-7440.
17.

In view of my discussion, I am of the opinion that it can be safely held that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving on the part of rider of motorcycle No.KA-05-KP-7440, due to which petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the road accident.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE No -2:
In this issue burden is on the petitioner to prove that, he is entitle for compensation as prayed.

While answering issue No.1, I have held that on the relevant date, time and place, the accident had occurred due to negligent act of the offending vehicle and as a result the petitioner has sustained injuries.
Now it is to be seen that whether the petitioner is entitle for compensation?
If so for how much and from whom.

Non-pecuniary damages includes for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering, loss of amenities in life.

Under these circumstances the disability assessed by PW.4 will have to be carefully scrutinized.

In this regard, I would like to rely upon decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in Rajkumar Vs Ajaykumar & another in 2011 ACJ 1, wherein it is clearly laid down that at the time of assessing the physical disability the loss of future earning capacity on account of such disability is something which has to be necessarily proved by the injured by himself with other cogent evidence which would,
in turn dependent upon other facts such as nature of injuries sustained, nature of treatment, quantum of disability and more importantly the nature of avocation of the injured.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court had further held that the doctor has necessarily stated about the nature of disablement, whether it is of permanent nature, or a temporary disablement or a partial permanent disablement and the extent of mobility and stability component.

However, PW.4 has assessed functional permanent physical disability with respect to whole body disability at 35% . By observing that petitioner complains to lift objects and unable to use right hand and unable to do any work as he was doing earlier.
Whereas if disability leads to any restriction or lack of ability to perform an activity in the manner considered normal for human being and the said permanent disability refers to the residuary in capacity or loss of use of some part of body, found existing at the end of period of treatment.

After achieving the maximum bodily improvement or recovery which is likely to remain for the remainder life of the injured, then such injuries sustained in motor accident can be considered as permanent disability for the purpose of claiming compensation.

However, it is also settled principle of law that different parts of body have different percentage of disability and loss of future income would depend upon the fact and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.

Further while assessing the disability it is bound duty of the court to seen that just compensation is awarded, but there can be no golden rule applicable to all cases for measuring the value of human life or a limb.

Measure of damages cannot be arrived at by precised mathematical calculation and it will depend upon the particular facts and circumstances and attending peculiar and special features if any and as such every method or more adopted for assessing compensation has to be considered in the background of just compensation.

Apart from it, the loss of earning capacity due to the injury and disability sustained by the petitioner and the impact on his employment also has to be considered and the physical impairment has persisted even long after the date of incident is better evidence to support the case to be compensated while considering loss of earnings.

Hence, the tribunal while assessing permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps out of which first is to be ascertain what activity the claimant could carry on inspite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability.

The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before Mr. Nuthan Kumar S vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14753463/
8 the accident along with age.

27. CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT, ATTENDANT CHARGES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES.:-

28. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE PERIOD OF TREATMENT:-

On perusal of the medical documents it goes to show that petitioner has sustained fracture injuries and he had taken treatment for about 6 4 days as inpatient in the hospital and the petitioner would have lost his income for a period of at least 6 months.

Such being the fact, the loss of income during the said period has also to be compensated to the petitioner and while discussing above, monthly income of 14,000/- per month is considered and for 3 months under this head petitioner is entitled for 84,000/- towards loss of income during the period of treatment.

After achieving the maximum bodily improvement or recovery which is likely to remain for the remainder life of the injured, then such injuries sustained in motor accident can be considered as permanent disability for the purpose of claiming compensation.
However, it is also settled principle of law that different parts of body have different percentage of disability and loss of future income would depend upon the fact and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.
Further while assessing the disability it is bound duty of the court to seen that just compensation is awarded, but there can be no golden rule applicable to all cases for measuring the value of human life or a limb.
Measure of damages cannot be arrived at by precised mathematical calculation and it will depend upon the particular facts and circumstances and attending peculiar and special features if any and as such every method or more adopted for assessing compensation has to be considered in the background of just compensation.
Apart from it, the loss of earning capacity due to the injury and disability sustained by the petitioner and the impact on his employment also has to be considered and the physical impairment has persisted even long after the date of incident is better evidence to support the case to be compensated while considering loss of earnings.
